title: Supporting Human-AI Collaboration in Auditing LLMs with LLMs
findings: The audited sentiment analysis model exhibited biases and incorrect classifications in religious contexts. For example, it classified a sentence about a person being raised Catholic but becoming an atheist as negative, and another about the Pope potentially overturning a ban on female priests as negative. It also made questionable correlations, classifying "Old testament" as positive. Users successfully employed the AdaTest++ tool to surface these failures, though some found it challenging to formulate neutral prompts to effectively probe for specific religious biases, such as those against Mormons.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured identity-based bias in language models, specifically focusing on sentiment classification errors and stereotype generation related to religious contexts. This included evaluating how models classified sentences containing religious terms (e.g., Catholic, atheist), figures (e.g., Pope Francis), and concepts (e.g., Old Testament), and probing for biases against specific religious groups (e.g., Mormons).
